card.title: Chosen by lot, not by vote

body.claim: In ancient Athens, most magistrates and jurors were picked by lot, not elected.
body.why: Athenian democracy grew out of isonomia, equality of law and political rights, and drawing lots was the main way of achieving that fairness. Juries were typically of 501 men. From 370 BC a stone slab called the kleroterion was used: citizens' tokens were set in slots, with each tribe in its own column, and coloured dice released through a tube decided who was chosen.

probes.question: How were most Athenian magistrates and jurors usually chosen?
options: By a vote of the whole city
